prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: AI and Decision-Making
area.rationale: Six candidates focus on integrating AI into decisions: strategic discipline, preserving human agency, irreplaceability of human judgment, building competence, risk‑based AI agency, and decision classification. They form a forward‑looking neighborhood on AI‑augmented decision‑making.

candidates.label: Strategic Discipline for AI-Augmented Decision-Making
candidates.description: Before integrating AI into decisions, organizations should treat decision-making as a strategic discipline and intentionally design human-machine relationships.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain why decision-making must be treated as a strategic discipline when adopting AI.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

candidates.label: Preserving Human Agency in AI Decisions
candidates.description: Maintain human agency by building accountability, ensuring decision-makers understand (not just comply with) AI outputs, and clearly connecting choices to choosers.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe at least two concrete ways to preserve human agency when AI supports decisions.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

candidates.label: Human Purpose and Judgment as Irreplaceable by AI
candidates.description: Technology can speed up analysis and reduce uncertainty, but it cannot substitute human purpose, values, and judgment behind choices.
coverage_criteria: Student can articulate at least one reason why human purpose and judgment remain essential even when AI provides analysis.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

candidates.label: Building Decision-Making Competence for Humans and AI
candidates.description: Organizations should simultaneously invest in developing human decision-making skills and rigorously measuring AI decision performance.
coverage_criteria: Student can describe one approach to improve human decision skill and one approach to measure AI decision performance.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

candidates.label: Risk-Based AI Agency Level
candidates.description: The degree of autonomy granted to AI agents should be calibrated according to the risk profile of the decision.
coverage_criteria: Student can justify why a high-risk decision warrants lower AI autonomy.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

candidates.label: Decision Classification Framework
candidates.description: Decisions can be categorized across multiple dimensions including risk, frequency, urgency, horizon, certainty, and the Cynefin domains. Understanding these dimensions helps in choosing appropriate decision strategies.
coverage_criteria: Student can name at least three decision dimensions and explain how the Cynefin context (Clear, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic) influences decision approach.
candidates.lesson_title: Decision-Making in the Age of AI

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
